bull_bear.body: Optimistic and confident; acknowledges near-term headwinds as temporary; emphasizes control over R&D, technology, and integration; highlights fast-tracking of high-margin products and long-term margin targets

bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The ~Rs 270 Cr Krystal Ingredients (Dahej) capex is being funded through a mix of internal accruals and debt.
- Shareholding as of 30th June 2026: Promoters 57.4%, Public 37.0%, DIIs 4.8%, FIIs 0.8%.
- Consolidated shareholders' funds grew from Rs 179.5 Cr (Mar-23) to Rs 449.9 Cr (Mar-26), alongside long-term borrowings that remained modest (Rs 21.7 Cr at Mar-26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated manufacturing platform with backward and forward integration, manufacturing flexibility and operational efficiency
- Dedicated in-house R&D centre with experienced scientists and advanced analytical capabilities, focused on process innovation, catalyst development, product customisation and high-value specialty molecules
- Advanced process technologies at the Dahej facility, including Continuous Flow and Vapor Phase Technology, Grignard's Reaction, amide coupling, Fridel Craft reactions, photochemical and cross coupling chemistries
- Diversified product portfolio across mint, clove, cooling agents, phenol derivatives and citral chemistry, reducing dependence on the traditional mint portfolio
- Diversified customer base across geographies with enduring relationships with several leading global flavour & fragrance companies and FMCG manufacturers
- Operating history since incorporation in 1997, evolving from an essential oils manufacturer into an integrated specialty ingredients company
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Feedstock and raw material price volatility — MD&A flags that the chemical industry continues to face challenges from feedstock volatility, and that volatility in commodity prices, freight costs and currencies continues to influence business operating environments across industries — directly relevant to a natural-feedstock-based ingredients maker.
- Tariff-related uncertainty and trade disruption in export markets — The Indian economy is described as navigating a volatile global environment marked by geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions and tariff-related uncertainties, with intensifying export competition also cited as a structural pressure in chemicals.
- Regulatory change across chemicals and food-contact applications — MD&A cites regulatory changes and regulatory pressures as a persistent industry challenge, and notes that evolving FSSAI food safety regulations are driving higher quality and product safety standards across the Indian food industry.
- Slowing global chemical cycle and supply-demand imbalance — Global chemical markets are expected to remain under pressure in 2026 following a turbulent 2025, with production growth forecast to moderate to 1.9% in 2026 from 2.6% in 2025, keeping the industry near the lower end of its business cycle.
- Structural weakness in Europe, a core flavour and fragrance market — Europe's chemical industry is projected to see only marginal recovery, with weak competitiveness, elevated energy costs, regulatory pressures and intensifying export competition weighing on the sector, while Europe remains the largest flavours and fragrances market.
- Energy price inflation and supply chain disruption — Rising energy prices, supply chain disruptions and continued geopolitical tensions in West Asia are named as key external risks to the Indian operating environment.
- Import dependence for select raw materials and high-value chemicals — MD&A flags India's dependence on imports for select raw materials and high-value chemicals as the driver of import substitution and domestic manufacturing investment, implying input-sourcing exposure for domestic manufacturers.
- Climate-related disruption to global commodity supply chains — The IMF-based outlook expects emerging and developing economies to face greater pressure from slowing growth, inflationary trends and climate-related disruptions affecting global commodity supply chains — a direct concern for botanical and natural feedstock availability.

business.body:
- One of the leading Indian manufacturers of specialty ingredients spanning essential oils, aroma chemicals and value-added derivatives, with 3 decades of experience, 80+ products across categories and 3 manufacturing facilities.
- Category leadership: largest processor of Clove Oil and Eugenol by volume in India (FY25) and largest processor of Eucalyptus Oil in India with ~58% market share (FY25), per Frost & Sullivan.
- Mint & Mint Derivatives is the largest, well-established segment (~65% of FY26 revenue, Rs 237 Cr), serving Oral Care, Pharma, Nutraceuticals, Personal Care and Wellness end-markets.
- India positioning by share of global supply (2025 industry study): ~53-55% in Cooling Agents, ~13% in Clove/Eugenol, and ~20-25% in Phenol Derivatives.
- Serves 240 domestic and 44 international customers across 20 countries; dōTERRA Enterprises, Sarl (USA) is both a strategic investor (since 2019) and customer.

The Company serves a diversified domestic and international customer base that includes several leading global flavour & fragrance companies and FMCG manufacturers.

outlook.body: Fast-tracking R&D pipeline (BHA, Eugenol derivatives) from FY27; import substitution in aroma chemicals; cross-selling Cooling Agents to existing Mint customers in confectionery; potential export expansion from Dahej plant
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Ramp up utilisation at the newly commissioned Dahej multipurpose facility as the central priority of the next phase of growth
- Reduce dependence on mint and mint derivatives by building a diversified, driver-led portfolio while continuing to grow leadership in the mint and mint derivatives business
- Scale up non-mint segments including citral and citral derivatives, cooling agents and phenol derivatives, backed by an advancing phenol derivatives development pipeline
- Accelerate commercialisation of new specialty molecules and keep investing in R&D to widen the specialty product pipeline
- Adopt advanced technologies such as continuous flow chemistry and vapor phase processes for higher yields, greater consistency, better cost competitiveness and more sustainable manufacturing
- Use the multipurpose plant's flexibility to pursue CRO, CMO and CDMO and custom manufacturing opportunities and build deeper partnerships with global clients
- Deepen relationships with global customers across flavour, fragrance, personal care and wellness applications
- Strengthen the supply chain through closer integration with raw material sources and improved logistics capabilities for responsiveness and cost efficiency
- Practise prudent capital allocation, having applied IPO proceeds towards partial debt repayment at Krystal Ingredients to reduce leverage and improve financial flexibility
- Maintain disciplined working capital management via improved inventory planning and close management of receivables, procurement cycles and supplier relationships
- Manage commodity and currency volatility through prudent raw material sourcing, a diversified supply base and active management of foreign exchange exposures
- Invest in workforce capability, training and a culture of safety, accountability and continuous improvement to manage increasing scale and complexity
- Pursue responsible growth with quality, safety and regulatory compliance aligned to global standards and ongoing efforts to improve process efficiency and reduce environmental impact
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The defining expansion of FY2025-26 was the commissioning of the greenfield multipurpose manufacturing facility at Dahej, which management describes as a key operational milestone and a step forward in the Company's manufacturing journey. Approximately Rs 270 crore was deployed towards the development of the Dahej facility; the investment expanded installed capacity to over 16,171 MTPA and takes the Company to three strategically located manufacturing plants at Silvassa, Budaun and Dahej. Designed with flexibility and scale in mind, the multipurpose plant strengthens process capabilities across multiple chemistries and was developed with advanced process technologies including Continuous Flow and Vapor Phase Technology, Grignard's Reaction, amide coupling, Fridel Craft reactions, photochemical reactions and cross coupling chemistries. Management positions it as enabling entry into high-value specialty molecules while strengthening backward and forward integration, manufacturing flexibility and operational efficiency, and as laying the foundation for diversification into higher-value specialty chemistries with an expanded specialty product portfolio and improved operating leverage; the successful execution is cited as evidence of the Company's project management capabilities and commitment to timely delivery. With the build complete, the stated forward agenda is not fresh capex but ramp-up and integration: driving operational excellence, supporting the ramp-up of the Dahej facility, and strengthening manufacturing and supply chain capabilities through closer integration with raw material sources and improved logistics. On funding, the utilisation of IPO proceeds towards partial debt repayment at Krystal Ingredients reduced leverage and improved financial flexibility.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Early signs of demand normalisation and stabilisation, with improving customer enquiries and order flows across both domestic and international markets
- Margins showed resilience, supported by stabilisation in mint prices, a more favourable product mix and continued cost discipline
- Higher depreciation following capitalisation of the Dahej facility is a non-cash charge; as utilisation levels improve, operating leverage is expected to strengthen and support margin expansion over the medium term
- With the major capital expenditure cycle nearing completion, the Company is entering a utilisation-led growth phase with progressive improvement expected in operating cash flows
- Higher asset utilisation is expected to enable better absorption of fixed costs and strengthen overall cash generation
- Tariff-related uncertainties in export markets and GST-related regulatory changes in the menthol segment influenced customer procurement behaviour and caused cautious demand during parts of the year
- Improved inventory planning, proximity advantages at the Dahej facility and reduced seasonality risk versus the mint value chain support efficient working capital deployment
- Non-mint capacity now significantly exceeds legacy mint-based capacity, a structural portfolio shift that strengthens long-term revenue visibility across demand cycles
- Long-term outlook described as firmly positive, supported by structural growth in end-use industries and increasing global demand for reliable, high-quality specialty ingredients
- Management states it tracks revenue growth, EBITDA margins, return on capital employed, operating cash flow generation and capital efficiency as the metrics of long-term value creation
- No order book is disclosed; management notes early signs of stabilisation supported by improving enquiry levels and gradual recovery in order flows across markets
- Improving customer enquiries and order flows across both domestic and international markets are cited as evidence of demand normalisation
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
